cards.note: No repository-plugins manifest was ever used: package.json already declares the surviving dsh.bundle.patch and the profile lists the package by name, so there is nothing to convert to an npm package.
No legacy dshClient field and no dsh.plugin.json manifest; the package has no client half whose declaration would have to move to dsh.client.
Host-side plugin only: no dsh.client declaration and no client bundle, so the client-modules scan never considers it.
Every consumed service is declared: the migration re-bound the inject array (apiProxy to llm) and reads it as ctx.llm.listProviders(); no ctx.get or property read of an undeclared service remains.

llm is a guaranteed profile service (mounted by @deepseek-ai/dsh-base), so the hard inject entry is correct rather than an optional-service over-dependency; the read itself keeps the documented best-effort try/catch degrade.
Subscribes to the provider-registry event llm/adapters-updated, not session/event, and derives no session state from event fields.
No Web Client half and no ctx.sessions use; there is no client-side session aggregation to move into the Node half.
Tails no task/run output and never calls tasks.peek or tasks.read, so no shadow accumulation buffer is needed.
Uses neither renamed service (httpServer/webServer, tasks/jobs) nor onTaskDone/onJobDone; the only service change here is apiProxy to llm, which is DSH-0.1.2-A1-01.
No ImageAttachmentRef, read_image use or persisted image metadata; the plugin reads one provider listing and logs it.
Does not register, wrap or parse read_image, and keeps no snapshots of its output.
No custom DeepSeek LLM adapter or image request interceptor; the provider-directory read carries no image payloads or file IDs.

Host-plane consumer: the removed apiProxy facade is replaced by the owning domain service (inject llm, ctx.llm.listProviders(), the same unary RPC as llm/listProviders) and the dead @deepseek-ai/dsh-host-apiproxy dependency is gone; the Remote envelope is not used on the host plane.
Target is alpha.2, so the temporary alpha.1 removal is superseded by DSH-0.1.2-A2-01; independently, the plugin produces no third-party persisted SessionEvents.
No host source patch to rebase and no internal session-view import; the plugin only injects the public llm service.
Contributes a bundle layer through the official dsh.bundle.patch/profile composer and never reads DSH_HOME or profile files itself, so no hardcoded profile path or removed demo package is involved.
No headless wrapper or stdout/stderr parser; the plugin logs through console.error from inside the host process.
Uses no tool presentation mode, PTC preset, dispatch waterfall or related types.
Carries no permission/approval policy, WebFetch preset or audit surface; it only reads the provider directory.
Registers no custom loopback HTTP/WS/RPC route, browser page or /api handler, so there is no channel to put behind the token/Cookie gate.
Not a model-provider plugin: it registers no provider login configuration and only reads the provider directory.
Ships no localization resources and carries no custom i18n patch; its Chinese console strings are debug output, not UI locale data.
No subagent orchestration or provider/model selector surface.
Informational/privacy note for deployments using the official adapter; the plugin needs no code change and is not a user-facing surface.
Carries no persistent PowerShell/Bash or Windows directory-picker workaround that the platform fixes could obsolete.
Does not enable session-log-deepseek and does not manage the delivery watermark; that opt-in belongs to the deployment profile, not to this bundle layer.
No browser acceptance script and no client bundle to look up in window.__DSH_BOOT__.entries; the plugin is proven by the headless boot probe.
Registers no structured-question answerer and touches no user-questions/request waterfall.
Infers no agent preset from a persisted session and sets no agent-presets roots.
No first-token detection or TPS computation and no @deepseek-ai/dsh-llm/message import.
The bundle layer inserts one row and restates no dsh-base row (telemetry or plugin inventory); the privacy stance belongs to the profile that lists it.
Imports no @earendil-works/pi-ai and no provider/auth package; after the migration the manifest is dependency-free.
No client half, no dsh.client.inject and no import of @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime to re-home.
Server-side entry only: the boot-manifest/client-registration keying does not apply, and the row id upgrade-demo is an ordinary Cordis entry id beside the package name.
Reads no session timeline or user message content, so the SessionBinding durable event window is not needed.
No composer DOM manipulation and no client code at all.
Does not render MarkdownText or fenced CodeBlocks from @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives.
Consumes no ctx.connection.api surface; history and transcript reads are not part of this plugin.
Constructs no subagent seed/persisted descriptor and consumes no subagent/descriptor event.
Calls no workspace navigation or directory-picker method (connectWorkspace, startSession, pickDirectory, listDirectory, createDirectory).
Produces no third-party persisted SessionEvent, so there is no ignorable marker to write or restore.
Host-plane call into the owning service, not a ctx.remote unary call, so there is no RemoteResult/RemoteError branch to handle.

Dependency graph audited for the target: the removed @deepseek-ai/dsh-host-apiproxy dependency is gone, the plugin imports no DSH package, and no peer is required (A2-08 session-projection does not name it); the manifest installs with no dependency resolution.
No startup wrapper or CI matrix and no Node-version workaround (forcing Node 22, skipping dsh web, probing the loader) to remove.
Does not consume pluginInventory/list or validate a PluginInventorySnapshot, so the optional agentPresets grouping is irrelevant to it.
No client half; it never called host.describe and does not read ctx.remote.$host.
Mounts no tool package and lists no peers; the profile dsh-base already mounts session-projection, and this row needs only the llm service.
Registers, reads or writes no settings namespace and imports no @deepseek-ai/dsh-settings symbol, so compile-time namespace validation does not touch it.
